Meeting header
Date: 2025-03-02 11:00am PT / 19:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM), Elena (AtlasPay Head of Security), Marcus (AtlasPay Procurement), Priya (AtlasPay Legal), Jonah (AtlasPay Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Align commercial lane and security path for a dedicated + private pilot in EU. Discuss MSA redlines, DPA terms around residency, KMS integration, and SLA targets. Pricing discussion around pilot fees vs committed capacity.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. can you all see the doc i just dropped in chat? it's the redwood onboarding checklist, i think i just put the soc2 and the basic msadpa bundle there.
[00:05] Elena: yep i can, and thanks. i'll flag, um, the keying piece is the big one for us. we need a bring-your-own-kms model or HSM-backed keys in eu. that's non-negotiable for atlass -- atlas pay.
[00:14] Liam: absolutely, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM. small note, currently we have two options: a private deployment where the control plane is customer-managed and we integrate to their KMS, or a Dedicated with BYOK using our key-wrapping approach. both can hit EU-residency, but there are tradeoffs on ops.
[00:24] Marcus: so for procurement, timeline matters. we need the pricing spelled out, like pilot cost, and then the committed reserved capacity rates. who signs the MSA first, and how long until we can get PO'd?
[00:33] Maya: good question. typical path is we route MSA -> DPA -> SOW if needed. we can provide a short pilot SOW for 30 days. pricing for pilot is usually a discounted reserved pool or a capped hosted trial, we'll put numbers in the pricing sheet after this call.
[00:43] Priya: i want to flag a couple of MSA redlines up front: data breach notification windows (we need 24 hours or less), subprocessor lists need pre-approval for key providers, and indemnity carve-outs for regulated txn data.
[00:56] Sofia: just to add, our standard MSA can accept a 24-48 hour notification timeline depending on severity. i'll make a note to include the SOC2 report and our incident playbook.
[01:05] Jonah: quick tech Q: latency for token gen in eu region with dedicated pool — we have p95 targets of about 120ms for the product flows. can redwood meet that with the KV cache enabled?
[01:15] Liam: in our benchmarks with sequence length typically under 512 tokens we can hit p95 ~90-140ms on a 4-GPU dedicated shard with continuous batching and prefix cache. caveat: quantization and model variant matter. also, the KV "cash" — sorry, kv cache — saves a lot on cost but slightly changes warmup.
[01:29] Elena: losing pronouns, but — okay. about encryption: where are the logs kept? audit logs need to stay in our VPC or at least be exportable to our SIEM. we can't have logs crossing regions without explicit control.
[01:40] Maya: logs are plumbed into the private control plane for Private deployments, and we offer log forwarding to your SIEM via a private peering or syslog over our VPC connector. for Hosted/Dedicated we provide audit logs but you asked for residency so Private is the more natural fit.
[01:52] Marcus: procurement will want the SLA spelled out, specifically uptime for the dedicated pool and a remedy schedule. what is your SLA for dedicated?
[02:00] Liam: our Dedicated product has an SLA template we can attach; typical uptime targets are 99.9% with credits for sustained outages, we also offer an escalation matrix. for strict production e2e latency SLOs we recommend Reserved capacity with burst buckets.
[02:12] Priya: also need clarity on data deletion on contract termination — is KV cache and model-context flushed? how long until customer data is irrecoverable?
[02:20] Sofia: we have retention settings. on Private, deletion is immediate by default per your retention policy; on Hosted we provide a 30-day purge window unless you opt for immediate purge and a BYOK/HSM which ensures keys are destroyed. we'll include the exact wording in the DPA redline.
[02:33] Elena: good. one more security ask: SSO/SAML with SCIM and RBAC. we need SAML group sync for roles and ability to limit who can request key rotations.
[02:43] Liam: supported. our console supports SAML + SCIM, and RBAC roles can be scoped per-organization, per-project. key rotation API is rate-limited and can be restricted to certain admin roles.
[02:54] Marcus: okay procurement question: cost path — is pilot invoiced up front or net-30 after trial? also how are egress/data-transfer fees handled?
[03:03] Maya: we do both depending on the enterprise procurement lane. pilots are often invoiced monthly net-30. egress fees are outlined in the rate card; for Private deployments there's usually no cross-region egress because it's inside your VPC, but for Hosted/Dedicated there can be transfer costs. we'll call those out in the pricing sheet.
[03:15] Priya: on the MSA, can you accept a mutual indemnity clause and a cap at three times the fees for direct damages? our legal team won't accept unlimited liability.
[03:25] Maya: mutual indemnity is typical; we can propose a limitation of liability clause. i'll loop product counsel and give you the baseline language we use.
[03:33] Jonah: technical: can we run a small benchmark using our sample workflows? we want to push typical request patterns with 2-step generation and streaming.
[03:40] Liam: yes, we'll set up a sandbox. i'll provide a perf script and a k6/gatling template. expect credentials via a secure share.
[03:47] Elena: question about subprocessor list — you said you integrate with cloud GPUs vendors, will we get a full supplier list? and how often is that updated?
[03:55] Sofia: yes we supply a subprocessor table and it's updated quarterly, with emergency notices if there's a change that affects residency or keying.
[04:03] Marcus: procurement timeline — we have a vendor window for approvals next week, is it realistic to get the MSA redline back and a demo by then?
[04:12] Maya: we'll aim to send our MSA template with suggested redlines by 2025-03-06, and liam can run the bench next week; the procurement window might need the sandbox perf results before final approval.
[04:20] Priya: i'm going to send a short doc with must-have DPA language and three absolute no-go points. i'll share that to your legal inbox.
[04:27] Maya: perfect. action recap — redwood provides SOC2, draft msadpa template, liam sets up EU sandbox, customer shares list of MSA no-go points and procurement contact.
[04:36] Elena: sounds good. any competitors we should watch? we did a quick bakeoff with BigCloud AI, they had lower upfront price but no BYOK on their hosted option.
[04:46] Maya: noted. we'll include a comparison sheet in the follow-up. thanks all, we'll follow up with the items in chat.
[04:50] (call ends, brief crosstalk and hangups)

Notes on transcript fidelity: occasional words misrecognized ("KV cash" for KV cache), timestamps approximate.
